title: Explain the editor host, then show its execution control
edits: Keep the title and plugin screenshot. Add a one-line host reminder beneath the existing setup instruction. Keep the visible question; do not turn this into a package-installation exercise.
copy:
Run editor scripts inside Unreal.

script: The language is still Python, but Unreal supplies the objects and editor functions. Our IDE can describe that API without running the editor. Before I execute anything, check this input field: is it in Python mode or console-command mode? What is unclear about where this code runs?
rationale: Prevents the common mistake of running an editor example in a normal terminal or putting the autocomplete stub on the runtime path.

rationale: Adds the missing practical execution detail without introducing debugger installation during class.

title: Use one blocked input to explain the existing validation
edits: Keep title, blue-cube result and protected-cube comparison. Replace the three bullets with the proposed sequence below. Replace the live duplicate-name attempt with a missing-texture attempt; keep duplicate-name behavior in optional study material. Do not modify texture settings during the demonstration.
copy:
Preview checks the texture set and target slot.
Apply creates one instance and changes one component.
Undo restores the assignment; the new asset remains.
What changes? What must stay unchanged?
script: First I have left one texture out. The tool blocks the operation before changing the scene. I will select the complete set and preview again. Check the destination, the texture mapping, the target and slot. After Apply, the blue cube changes and the protected cube stays plain. We inspect the actual parameter state as well as the message. Undo restores the assignment, but it does not remove the new instance asset. What questions do you have about those two results?
rationale: Uses an existing failure path to teach validation, state inspection and recovery. Karol’s texture fixer is not copied into an actor-only tool that promises to leave shared inputs unchanged.
timing: Same 7 minutes / 3:49–3:56: 0:00–0:45 prediction; 0:45–1:30 missing-input block and correction; 1:30–3:00 Preview/Apply; 3:00–4:15 result/protected scope; 4:15–5:15 Undo and retained asset; 5:15–7:00 questions and recovery buffer.
layout: Keep the existing actual result image. Use the existing native preview capture in the run sheet while demonstrating inputs. No new blocked-state capture is claimed.

Three tagged anchors → three prepared effects.

title: Keep the prefix lab, strengthen its technical evidence
edits: Keep the exact-one-SM_ rule and existing lab structure. Add the expected untouched set to the instructor answer guide, not another student implementation task. A success-count message is insufficient evidence.

title: Turn a confirmed defect into a regression check
edits: Keep title, Observe → Interpret → Revise → Retest loop and peer-test question. Add an optional study pointer, “Explore further: from a confirmed defect to a regression test.” Do not replace peer testing with an automation lecture.
copy:
Observe the attempt → investigate the cause → revise → retest.
A confirmed defect can become a repeatable regression check.
What questions remain before you write the peer-test task?
script: A useful observation names the input, action, expected result and what actually happened. Once we confirm a defect, we can turn the repeatable part into a regression check. For example, an incomplete texture set must not create an asset. That automated check still cannot tell us whether a new artist understands the error message. What questions remain before you write your peer-test task?
rationale: Separates correctness evidence from usability evidence while giving student observations a practical engineering destination.
timing: Use 30–40 seconds inside anchor 16E’s existing 3:30; retain the final question pause and all peer-testing time.
layout: Keep the loop visual. Add a discreet optional link to the existing test example; no new live slide.
